title: Lambda Dead Letter Queue Depth and Message Rate

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.5.10 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.5.10 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudwatch` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" namespace="AWS/SQS" metric_name="ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible"
| table _time metric_name namespace unit average maximum
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.5.10_lambda_dead_letter_queue_10"
| sort -_time
description: Messages landing in DLQs mean unprocessed events—often billing, inventory, or security actions—until replayed or dropped.
value: Detecting lambda dead letter queue depth and message rate early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Tag or name DLQ queues consistently (`*dlq*`). Ingest SQS CloudWatch metrics per queue. Correlate queue to owning Lambda via Event Source Mapping inventory (lookup table). Alert on any sustained visible message count or sudden spikes after bad deployments.
visualization: Single value (DLQ depth), Line chart (visible messages by queue), Table (QueueName, linked function, visible).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` avg(Performance.cpu_load_percent) as agg_value
  from datamodel=Performance where nodename=Performance.CPU
  by Performance.host span=5m
| sort - agg_value
dataModelAcceleration: Enable data model acceleration for Performance (CPU node).
knownFalsePositives: Cold starts, retries, and a bad client sending junk traffic can all raise error counts without a code bug. We look at the share of invocations and we compare the same time last week before we assume the function is broken.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:cloudwatch`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.5.16.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `metric_name` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Tag or name DLQ queues consistently (`*dlq*`). Ingest SQS CloudWatch metrics per queue. Correlate queue to owning Lambda via Event Source Mapping inventory (lookup table). Alert on any sustained visible message count or sudden spikes after bad deployments.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" namespace="AWS/SQS" metric_name="ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible"
| table _time metric_name namespace unit average maximum
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.5.10_lambda_dead_letter_queue_10"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudwatch` in `index=aws` to detect lambda dead letter queue depth and message rate. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the Amazon CloudWatch console Metrics for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `metric_name` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_5_10_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Single value (DLQ depth), Line chart (visible messages by queue), Table (QueueName, linked function, visible)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of lambda dead letter queue depth and message rate so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
